title: I’m making a card game that mixes RPG party building with roguelike autobattles
author: NightwoodStudios
selftext:
I wanted to share the game I’ve been working on since August. It’s called Into The Nightwood, and it’s a mix of an autobattler, RPG, roguelike and card game. You put together a party of heroes, build them up with abilities and equipment, and try to survive your way through the Nightwood.

I’ve put hundreds of hours into it so far and there’s still a lot more to go. I’ve reworked it more times than I can count with 8,935 prompts used so far. The whole process has been really fun and let me really test my creativity.

The biggest headache by far has been balancing. I want it to be difficult enough that winning feels good, without it feeling unfair or frustrating. But there are so many things I can tweak between the heroes, monsters, abilities, equipment, talents, progression and drop rates. Then I change something and have to figure out what that’s done to everything else.

I started working on balance over a month ago. I’ve changed how I’m approaching it several times and I still feel like I’m only a small way towards where I want it to be but I do finally feel like I have a good process.

It hasn’t helped that my PC has limited storage, CPU and RAM. I can only run so many testing workers at once, so getting through the test runs and seeing whether the changes actually helped has been slow. There’s been a lot of waiting, checking results, adjusting things and going again.

I’m sure some people will call it “AI slop” when it comes out. I know using AI will put some people off, but I really am pouring my heart and soul into this game. I want to make something people enjoy spending time in when it is finally done.

The next thing I need to figure out is marketing. I’ve spent so much time working on the game, and now I’m trying to work out how to let people know it even exists. I am working on a demo at the moment but I am not sure if I should get this out as soon as it's ready or wait until the next fest in February and release it with that. If anyone here has been through this with their own game, I’d love to hear how you found your first players.

If it looks like something you’d enjoy, [please give Into The Nightwood a wishlist on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5528540/). I’d really appreciate it.

Happy to hear any feedback on the game, trailer, steam page ect... and chat about the game or how I’ve been using AI to build.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/NightwoodStudios please add details on how AI was used to make this. Just stating that you used AI doesn't pass the rule. The community is a dev community, add dev details. Rule 4 is there to make sure promotional posts contribute by getting into the process and actual development. There's a real risk of the sub being swamped by self-promotion. If you don't update, this post may be removed.

replies.author: NightwoodStudios
replies.body: Edited my post with a bit more detail on how I am approaching balancing.

replies.author: NightwoodStudios
replies.body: Any specific bits that stick out? Or changes you would make to improve the style?

comments.author: Beneficial_Feed_2595
comments.body:
The art style has 

1.) No unique identity.  
2.) overly detailed so that the eye is overwhelmed.

That is what makes it slop.

replies.author: NightwoodStudios
replies.body: Thank you for your feedback. I like the art style but it is clear it's a turn off for everyone that's posted here. I may look into changing it but I'm not sure what direction to go if I want to avoid a pixel style.

comments.author: CashFirm573
comments.body: Good luck, did you bother to check how many AI games coming out every month that same 5 genres? well good luck cause you won't sell anything. Art work alone is so bad I think people will block ya game.

replies.author: NightwoodStudios
replies.body: Thank you for your feedback. I like the art style but it's clear that is a turn off for everyone here that has seen it so I may reconsider it. I know the market is being flooded with ai games. I have not seen any exactly like this which is why I built it but it is hard to see everyone one coming out. My target is to sell just enough to cover the ai costs but I know that might be ambitious.
